points: In the tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day, the word came to set Ezekiel's face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers and says, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: The Most High will put hooks in his jaws, bring him up out of his rivers, and leave him thrown in the wilderness, because Egypt has been a staff of reed to the house of Israel that broke and tore their shoulder when they leaned upon it.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: The Most High will bring a sword upon Egypt, cut off man and beast, and make the land utterly waste and desolate from Syene to the border of Ethiopia, uninhabited forty years, scattering the Egyptians among the nations.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: At the end of forty years He will bring the Egyptians again from where they were scattered into the land of Pathros, but they shall be a base kingdom, the basest of kingdoms, no more to rule over the nations or be the confidence of the house of Israel.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: In the twenty-seventh year the word came that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to serve a great service against Tyrus, yet had no wages for it, every head made bald and every shoulder peeled.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: Therefore the Most High gives the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for his army, because they wrought for Him; in that day the horn of the house of Israel will bud forth and Ezekiel will be given the opening of the mouth in their midst.
